title: Ζεὺς καὶ Ἀπόλλων
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 121 (= Perry 104). Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ζεὺς καὶ Ἀπόλλων περὶ τοξικῆς ἤριζον.
sentences.tr: Zeus kai Apollōn peri toxikēs ērizon.
sentences.l: Zeus and Apollo were contending about archery.
sentences.n: τοξική is feminine because τέχνη, 'art', is understood with it, as in μουσική and ῥητορική. The contest is on Apollo's own ground: he is the archer god, and the bow is his emblem.

sentences.t: Τοῦ δὲ Ἀπόλλωνος ἐντείναντος τὸ τόξον καὶ τὸ βέλος ἀφέντος, Ζεὺς τοσοῦτον διέβη ὅσον Ἀπόλλων ἐτόξευσεν.
sentences.tr: Tou de Apollōnos enteinantos to toxon kai to belos aphentos, Zeus tosouton diebē hoson Apollōn etoxeusen.
sentences.l: And when Apollo had drawn the bow and let the arrow go, Zeus stepped across just so far as Apollo had shot.
sentences.n: Another genitive absolute, and a double one — two participles on the one noun. ἐντείνω is to stretch the bow taut. τοσοῦτον … ὅσον is the correlative pair of extent, so much as. The joke is that Zeus never shoots: he answers the arrow with one step, and the match is over.

sentences.t: Οὕτως οἱ τοῖς κρείττοσιν ἀνθαμιλλώμενοι, πρὸς τῷ ἐκείνων μὴ ἐφικέσθαι, καὶ γέλωτα ὀφλισκάνουσιν.
sentences.tr: Houtōs hoi tois kreittosin anthamillōmenoi, pros tōi ekeinōn mē ephikesthai, kai gelōta ophliskanousin.
sentences.l: Thus those who match themselves against their betters, besides not reaching those men, incur ridicule as well.
sentences.n: πρὸς τῷ with an articular infinitive is 'in addition to' doing something, and the negative μή sits inside the infinitive phrase. ὀφλισκάνω γέλωτα is a courtroom metaphor: to lose one's case and owe the penalty. What such a man is sentenced to pay is laughter. ἀνθαμιλλάομαι carries the ἀντι- of setting oneself opposite an opponent; ἐφικνέομαι takes the genitive of the mark reached.
